title: Facilitating Singaporeans Entering Malaysia to Take Care of Essential Personal Matters
what_it_is: Facilitating Singaporeans Entering Malaysia to Take Care of Essential Personal Matters

sections.label: Travel help for Singaporeans
sections.summary: Since March 2020, Singapore facilitated travel for over 250 appeal cases and repatriated over 350 stranded Singaporeans, with an in-principle agreement on travel protocols.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Since March 2020, we have helped to facilitate travel for more than 250 appeal cases from Singapore Citizens or PRs who wanted to enter Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have also facilitated the repatriation of more than 350 Singaporeans who were stranded in Malaysia, and these were usually the elderly or very young, or people with disability and mobility issues, and we have had to run special services across the Causeway to bring our people back home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have reached with the Malaysian authorities an in-principle agreement to have protocols for travel in such circumstances, including family bereavements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The exact details are still being worked out.

sections.label: Malaysia immigration approval process
sections.summary: For each case, Singapore informs the person to get approval from Malaysia's Director-General of Immigration, who holds final discretion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I wonder if the Minister could share with us his observations about how functional currently are the diplomatic channels to resolve bilateral issues.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I said just now we had facilitated more than 250 cases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: For each case that MFA is aware of, we would first inform the Singaporean or PR concerned that they need to get approval – specific approval from the Director-General of Immigration of Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We always ask them to keep us informed so that we can also reach out informally to the Malaysian High Commission to try our best to persuade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But the legal and diplomatic position is that the ultimate discretion and the final decision rest with the Director-General of Immigration of Malaysia.

sections.label: Formal and informal diplomatic communications
sections.summary: Formal and informal communications, including WhatsApp messages and personal calls, are flowing, and the Malaysian official has obliged.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, all those ties, those communications, both formal and informal, including WhatsApp messages, are flowing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I can tell you that there have been occasions where I have even had to call him up personally because a Singaporean got stuck in a particularly delicate situation and he has obliged.
